title: WPMS/1926/2011 of TABASSUM KHAN Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 1926 (MS) of 2011
Tabassum Khan ...Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ...Respondents
Ms. Tabassum Khan, petitioner present in person.
Mr. Subhash Upadhyay, Brief Holder present for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Bhaskar Chandra Joshi, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Vipul Sharma,
Advocate present for respondent no. 3.
Mr. Ajay Singh Bisht, Advocate for respondent no. 4.
Mr. B.D. Upadhyay, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Sunil Upadhyay, Advocate
present for the Kumaon University.
Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. Heard Ms. Tabassum Khan, petitioner in person,
Mr. Subhash Upadhyay, Brief Holder for the State of
Uttarakhand, Mr. Bhaskar Chandra Joshi, Advocate
holding brief of Mr. Vipul Sharma, Advocate for
respondent no. 3, Mr. Ajay Singh Bisht, Advocate for
respondent no. 4, Mr. B.D. Upadhyay, Senior Advocate
assisted by Mr. Sunil Upadhyay, Advocate for the
Kumaon University.
2. The petitioner is a student of B.H.M.S. (i.e. Bachelor
of Homeopathic Medicine and Surgery) in an institute
known as "Chandola Homeopathic Medical College and
Hospital", Kichchha Road, Rudrapur, District Udham
Singh Nagar. The petitioner has completed second year of
B.H.M.S. from the said institute. She seeks migration to
another Homeopathic College, inter alia, on grounds that
facilities in the said institute are not upto mark.
3. Homeopathic Colleges are under regulation of a
Central Body known as "Central Council for
Homeopathic", New Delhi. Regulations have been framed
by the said Regulatory Body under which migration from

2
one Homeopathic Medical College to another, even from
one Homeopathic College which is in one University to a
Homeopathic Medical College, which is under a different
University can be made but only by the Central Body (i.e.
Central Council for Homeopathic, New Delhi). The
petitioner seeks migration from "Chandola Homeopathic
Medical College and Hospital" Kichchha Road, Rudrapur,
District Udham Singh Nagar, to a nearby Homeopathic
Medical College, namely, State K.G.K. Homeopathic
Medical College, Moradabad, which is in the
neighbouring, State of Uttar Pradesh. It must also be
noted here that the student here has little choice in this
matter as in the State of Uttarakhand there is no other
Homeopathic Medical College other than the one where
she is presently undergoing her studies and from where
she appears to be totally dissatisfied.
4. All the same, since the necessary documents were
not being forwarded by the College, this Court in its order
dated 26.12.2011 directed the college to forward the
necessary papers to the University i.e. Kumaon
University. Order passed on 26.12.2011 reads as under:
1. Heard Ms. Tabassum Khan, petitioner in
person, Mr. H.M. Raturi, Standing Counsel for
the State of Uttarakhand, Mr. Vipul Sharma,
Advocate for respondent no. 3, Mr. Ajay Singh
Bisht, Advocate for respondent no. 4, Mr. B.D.
Upadhyay, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr.
Sunil Upadhyay, Advocate for the Kumaon
University and Ms. Beena Pande, Standing
Counsel for the State of Uttar Pradesh.
2. Before this Court is a student who has
appeared in person, who has already
completed two years course in Bachelor of
Homeopathic Medicine and Surgery (from
hereinafter referred to as B.H.M.S.) from a
college known as "Chandola Homeopathic
Medical College, Rudrapur, Udham Singh

3
Nagar. Now she needs migration to another
Homeopathic College for the reason that this
college does not have enough facilities. She
relied upon various reports of State
Government as well as report of Family
Welfare, Department of AYUSH Homeopathic,
Education Section, Red Cross Road, New Delhi
(respondent no. 4) to strengthen the argument
about the state of affairs in the said
Homeopathic Medical College.
3. In the Counter affidavit filed by
respondent no. 4 i.e. Union of India, Ministry
of Health, Family Welfare, Department of
AYUSH Homeopathic Education Section, Red
Cross Road, New Delhi in paragraph-12 it is
admitted that the college does not have
infrastructure to hold the course of B.H.M.S.,
which reads as follows:
 "That in reply to the contents of
Paragraph no. 13 of the writ petition it is
submitted that the college does not have
required teaching faculty staff as provided
under the Homeopathic (MSE) Regulation
1983. The answering respondent neither have
any role in the migration of Medical students
nor it have any objection if the Hon'ble court
direct so to respondent Nos. 1 & 5."
4. The regulation pertaining to migration of
student in such Homeopathic College is
governed by regulation (v), which reads as
follows:-
"(v) Transfer of students from One College to
another:
(a) A student studying in a Homeopathic
Medical College may be allowed to
migrate/transfer to another Homeopathic
Medical College under same or another
University.
(b) The University concerned can allow the
migration/ transfer within three months after
passing the First BHMS examination, as a
rule.
(c) Migration/Transfer of students during the
course of their training for the clinical subjects
may be avoided.
(d) The number of students
migrating/transferring from one college to
another college during one year will be kept to

4
the minimum so that the training of the
regular students of that college is not adversely
affected. The number of students migrating/
transferring to/ from anyone college should
not exceed the limit of 5% of its intake subject
to a maximum of 5 student in anyone
Homeopathy college in one year.
(e) Cases not covered under the above
regulations may be referred to the Council
for consideration on individual merits.
(f) Intimation about the admission of migrated/
transferred students into any College shall be
sent to the Council forthwith."
5. Although the petitioner has already
undergone the first two examinations and her
case would be covered under clause (v) (e).
Though according to the Central Council of
Homeopathic, further process has to start by
the concerned Medical College and the
concerned University. Since delay has already
been caused by the said Medical College and
the Kumaon University, the college is hereby
directed to forward the entire papers of the
petitioner, the same shall be forwarded to the
Kumaon University. Mr. B.D. Upadhyay,
Senior Advocate appearing for the Kumaon
University undertakes that if these papers are
received by the University the same shall be
promptly forwarded to Central Council of
Homeopathic, "Jawahar Lal Nehru Bhartiya
Chikitsa Evam Homeopathic Anusandhan
Bhawan", at their address at 61-65
Institutional Area, Opp. 'D' block, Janakpuri,
New Delhi-110058. Needful shall be done
within a period of one week from the date of
receipt of the papers from Chandola
Homeopathic Medical College and Hospital,
Kichchha road, Rudrapur, District Udham
Singh Nagar.
7. List this petition on 9.1.2012 in the daily
cause list."
5. Today i.e. on 9.1.2012, when the matter has come
up before this Court, a statement has been made by Mr.
Bhaskar Chandra Joshi, Advocate holding brief of Mr.
Vipul Sharma, Advocate appearing for the "Chandola

5
Homeopathic Medical College" that in compliance of the
direction of this Court, the papers relating to migration of
petitioner have been forwarded to the Kumaon University
and the college (i.e. "Chandola Homeopathic Medical
College and Hospital") has no objection if the petitioner is
migrated to another college.
6. The Kumaon University is being represented before
this Court by Senior Advocate Mr. B.D. Upadhyay, who
has admitted that the University has received all the
documents pertaining to migration of the petitioner, and
without any further delay the documents will be
forwarded to the regulatory body i.e. Central Council of
Homeopathic, Jawahar Lal Nehru Bhartiya Chikitsa
Evam Homeopathic Anusandhan Bhawan, Jankpuri, New
Delhi. Mr. B.D. Upadhyay, Senior Advocate undertakes
that the needful will be done on or before 12.1.2012.
7. Under the regulations, however, the final decision
has to be taken by respondent no. 5, i.e. President,
Central Council of Homeopathic, New Delhi. It is hereby
directed that since the entire career of a student is at
stake, a prompt decision needs to be taken by
respondent no. 5 regarding migration of the petitioner
from "Chandola Homeopathic Medical College and
Hospital" to another medical college. Since efforts are
already being made by the petitioner to get admission in
State K.G.K. Homeopathic Medical College, Moradabad,
Uttar Pradesh (in case the rules permit), formalities must
be completed as expeditiously as possible.
8. Since the State K.G.K. Homeopathic Medical
College, Moradabad is in the State of Uttar Pradesh,

6
respondent no. 7, i.e. the Principal Secretary (Medical
Education), Medical Health and Family Welfare,
Government of Uttar Pradesh, Lucknow is also requested
to facilitate the migration of the petitioner to the said
medical college, if the same is permissible under the law,
and more importantly if the President of the Central
Council of Homeopathic, New Delhi (respondent no. 5),
agrees for the same.
9. With the above observations, writ petition is
disposed of.
10. No order as to costs.
11. Certified copy of this order be issued within a period
of 24 hours.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
Dated: 9.1.2012
Virendra
